claims.harm: Interrupted in-place writes could corrupt data files without atomic updates or checksum detection
claims.quote: How worried are we about file corruption here? I thought the main reason we use leveldb and sqlite databases in places like this where we don't need indexing is that they support atomic updates, so you can pull the power cord any time and next time you reboot you will will see some consistent view of the data
claims.settled_by_quote: The latest push updates the block tree store to use a write ahead log for atomic writes, and crc32c checksums to detect data corruption.

claims.harm: Directory committing is a no-op on Windows, potentially breaking flag file atomicity and leading to inconsistencies on power loss
claims.quote: This is a no-op on Windows. I think this can lead to several edge case issues, like the block tree being marked as unpruned when blocks have already been removed, or the WAL not being applied atomically.

claims.harm: READ-mode readers could observe stale or partially applied data if a writer crashed leaving an unapplied WAL
claims.quote: since READ-mode methods then read the data files directly, a reader could observe stale or partially applied data if log_flag.dat is present from a failed writer. Is that OK in this use-case?

support.reason: The codebase changes seem surprisingly small for this proposal. Changing the code to reduce the dependency on LevelDB sounds good to me.
Allows parallel index building in tools like Electrs and Esplora via libbitcoinkernel without requiring Bitcoin Core to be stopped
Interested in replacing the LevelDB dependency for block and header metadata
Excited about replacing LevelDB dependency in kernel and tested on signet
Differentially fuzzed BlockTreeDB and BlockTreeStore for ~5000 cpu hours with no issues

result.notes: Initial assessment confirmed strong conceptual support for moving away from LevelDB for block index storage. Two non-blocking technical objections remain open regarding Windows directory syncing and READ-mode handling of pending WALs; author converted PR to draft to redesign parallel reader access and log application.
